title: MEMO: Memory-Augmented Model Context Optimization for Robust Multi-Turn Multi-Agent LLM Games
claim: Our method simultaneously achieves higher performance, better stability, and far greater sample efficiency than competing prompt-optimization and RL baselines.
layout: 2 side-by-side scatter/line plots; green arrow toward ours; labeled baselines
description: Two side-by-side plots under a light-blue banner with a code link. Panel (a), 'Stability vs. Mean win-rate', is a scatter plot with relative standard error on the x-axis and mean win-rate on the y-axis. Baselines (MIPRO, TextGrad, GEPA, CoT, ToT, Baseline) are small colored dots in the lower middle and right. The blue star labeled 'MEMO (Ours)' sits alone at the top left. A green curved arrow points toward it, showing the direction of improvement. Panel (b), 'Efficiency vs. KuhnPoker Mean win-rate', plots win-rate against number of games on a log-like x-axis. A bold blue line with diamond markers rises steeply to 0.60 by 2,000 games. Grey RL squares climb slowly to about 0.53 by 50,000 games. GEPA, MIPRO and TextGrad appear as single triangles, and a red Baseline point and line sit at 0.45. Bold captions sit below each panel.
caption: Left Run-to-run performance and stability comparison. Using GPT-4o-mini with MEMO achieves the highest mean win rate (49.5%) with the lowest RSE (6.4%). Right Learning efficiency comparison against the self-play RL baseline method UNSTABLEBASELINE. Using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, MEMO reaches 60% win rate on Kuhn Poker with only 2,000 games, 19× fewer than the 38,000 games required by the RL self-play baseline.
abstract: Multi-turn, multi-agent LLM game evaluations often exhibit substantial run-to-run variance. In long-horizon interactions, small early deviations compound across turns and are amplified by multi-agent coupling. This biases win rate estimates and makes rankings unreliable across repeated tournaments. Prompt choice worsens this further by producing different effective policies. We address both instability and underperformance with MEMO (Memory-augmented MOdel context optimization), a self-play framework that optimizes inference-time context by coupling retention and exploration. Retention maintains a persistent memory bank that stores structured insights from self-play trajectories and injects them as priors during later play. Exploration runs tournament-style prompt evolution with uncertainty-aware selection via TrueSkill, and uses prioritized replay to revisit rare and decisive states. Across five text-based games, MEMO raises mean win rate from 25.1% to 49.5% for GPT-4o-mini and from 20.9% to 44.3% for Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, using $2,000$ self-play games per task. Run-to-run variance also drops, giving more stable rankings across prompt variations. These results suggest that multi-agent LLM game performance and robustness have substantial room for improvement through context optimization. MEMO achieves the largest gains in negotiation and imperfect-information games, while RL remains more effective in perfect-information settings. All code is open-source and available here: https://github.com/openverse-ai/MEMO
